evidence: M-O s.v. play (a piece of music or other recording), citing Curt. 3.10.7
Quint. 11.2.1: memoriae vīs repraesentat aliquid (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically to bring something before the eyes or mind, to show or exhibit it (Quint., Curt., Plin.; Lewis & Short); Morgan–Owens uses it for playing music or a film.
Andresian labels the play button with it: classically to push or strike (Lewis & Short), as the lexicon’s push.
Classically “make use of”; the sense “play (a recording)” is Traupman’s.

sources: Lewis & Short: repraesento · Lewis & Short: impello · Lewis & Short: usurpo
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. play (a piece of music or other recording …).
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 361.
